title: Toxicity Screens in Human Retinal Organoids for Pharmaceutical Discovery
protocol: Coat a 6-well cell culture plate with basement membrane matrix medium.
Dilute 75 µL cold matrix medium with 9 mL of DMEM/F12 to make 1x medium.
Add 1.5 mL of freshly prepared 1x medium per well in a 6-well plate and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
Aspirate off the basement membrane matrix medium and rinse each well with 3 mL of DMEM/F12.
Add 2 mL of DMEM/F12 and incubate at 37 °C until use.
Use the plate the day it is prepared.
Prepare a 10 mM stock solution of rock inhibitor (Y-27632 dihydrochloride) in PBS, and store at -20 °C until use.
Thaw a vial of iPSCs/ESCs into DMEM/F12 medium and centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in mTeSR medium.
Plate 1 vial of cells on to a coated 6-well well in mTeSR media with 10 µM of rock inhibitor (Y-27632 dihydrochloride) and incubate overnight in the incubator.
Aspirate off media and add back just mTeSR the next day.
Prepare 0.5 mM EDTA in PBS by diluting 500 µL of 0.5 M EDTA in 500 mL of PBS.
Passage cells when they reach 80-90% confluency.
Split cells 1:3 or 1:6 per well, depending on the growth rate of the cells.
Aspirate off media from the plate.
Incubate with 0.5 mM EDTA in PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove EDTA solution and lift off cells by forcefully ejecting 1 mL of mTeSR medium onto cells with a p1000 pipette.
Suck up and forcefully eject mTeSR medium and cells, up to 5 times, to remove the adhered remaining cells.
Plate cells onto a fresh basement membrane matrix-coated 6-well plate with mTeSR medium.
Continue replacing media daily until plates reach 80-100% confluency.
Set aside one well for cell line expansion or cryopreservation once confluency is reached.
Use the remaining five wells to begin the differentiation process by making embryoid bodies.
Prepare a 5x stock solution of Dispase by dissolving powder in DMEM/F12.
Sterile filter the 5x Dispase solution using a 0.22 μm filter.
Store 1 mL aliquots at -20 °C until use.
Using the 5x Dispase solution, prepare 1 mL/well of 2 mg/mL Dispase in DMEM/F12.
Warm the Dispase solution at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Supplement DMEM/F12 with 1% N2 supplement, 1% MEM NEAA, and 2 mg/mL heparin at 180 U/mg to prepare NIM.
Store prepared NIM at 4°C for up to one month.
Mix 16 mL of mTeSR:NIM (12mL:4mL) solution and warm it to room temperature.
Remove differentiated cells from the culture wells using a p10 pipette tip under a dissection scope.
Aspirate off mTeSR medium from the culture wells, removing differentiated clumps.
Add pre-warmed Dispase solution immediately after aspirating the mTeSR medium.
Incubate at 37°C until most edges of cell colonies begin to curl up under a microscope (4-8 min).
Aspirate the Dispase solution and gently add back at least 2 mL of DMEM/F12 medium per well slowly to the side of the well.
Aspirate DMEM/F12 medium from the cells.
Forcefully add fresh 1 mL of DMEM/F12 directly onto the cells to lift cell colonies.
Use a p1000 pipette to repeatedly suck up and forcefully eject DMEM/F12 in the well, up to 5 times, to dislodge as many cell colonies as possible.
Transfer floating colonies to a 15 mL conical tube.
Rinse wells with an additional 1 mL DMEM/F12 medium per well to collect any remaining floating colonies.
Allow the floating colonies to settle by gravity for no more than 5 minutes.
Remove all but 1-2 mL of supernatant carefully without disturbing the soft pellet at the bottom.
Resuspend the pellet in pre-warmed 3:1 mTeSR:NIM medium.
Transfer the resuspended cells to an ultra-low-attachment T75 flask.
Incubate overnight to allow EBs to form, which is considered Day 0 of differentiation.
Remove media from free-floating EB culture by tipping the flask up and aspirating off the supernatant without disturbing the EBs in the pellet.
Replace the media with 10 mL of 1:1 mTeSR:NIM medium.
The following day, replace the media with 10 mL of 1:3 mTeSR:NIM medium.
The next day, replace the media with full NIM medium.
Continue changing media every 2 days with NIM medium until 7 days following Dispase treatment.
Plate free-floating EBs onto a 6-well plate coated with growth factor-reduced basement membrane matrix medium one week after Dispase treatment.
Aspirate spent media from EBs and replace with 12 mL of NIM.
Ensure an even distribution of EBs into each well by agitating the EB-containing media to resuspend the EBs, then quickly remove 2 mL and dispense into one well.
Repeat for the remaining wells.
Before incubating, gently shake the plate back and forth then side to side to evenly distribute the EBs.
Change the media daily with NIM medium.
Maintain the level of media in the wells at approximately 3 mL.
Remove all but 1 mL of media when changing media to prevent drying out the plated EBs.
Add 2 mL of media gently to the side of the well during media change.
Nine days after plating EBs, start switching media from NIM to Retinal Differentiation Media (RDM) over two days.
Prepare RDM by mixing 48% DMEM/F12 (1:1), 48% DMEM with supplements including B27 without vitamin A, MEM NEAA, and Pen-Strep.
Filter sterilize the prepared RDM using a 0.20 μm filter.
Store RDM at 4°C for up to one month.
Switch media to a 1:1 mix of NIM and RDM on the first day of transitioning.
Change the media entirely to RDM on the second day.
Feed cells with RDM on all subsequent days.
Fragment plated EBs at 28 days following initial Dispase treatment using a sterile scalpel to create a 1-2 mm² grid.
Add 2 mL of RDM to each well.
Aspirate approximately 1000 µL of media from the wells using a p1000 pipette.
Eject the aspirated media directly onto plated EBs with the tip fully submerged.
Repeat the ejection process until all cells are lifted from the plate.
Resuspend detached EB chunks in a sterile plastic 125 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Fill the flask with approximately 40 mL of RDM media.
Place the flask on an orbital shaker set at 130-140 RPM (speed setting 3).
Feed organoids by performing partial media changes, replacing approximately 12 mL of RDM 2-3 times per week.
Prune organoids every two weeks to remove non-retinal, overgrown, and dying organoids.
Transfer cells from their flask onto a 6-well plate or 10 cm dish using a 5 mL pipette.
Keep organoids that display stratified neuroepithelium.
Sort out and remove ill-formed or overgrown retinal organoids with a 5 mL pipette.
Remove non-retinal organoids that are opaque and yellowish.
Maintain mature organoids by changing the media to RDM+ at day 56 following initial Dispase treatment.
Prepare 100 mM taurine in PBS.
Store aliquots of taurine in -20 °C until use.
Supplement RDM with 10% FBS, 100 µM Taurine, and 2 mM commercial glutamine supplement to prepare RDM+.
Filter sterilize the supplemented media using a 0.20 µm filter.
Change RDM+ media 2-3 times a week.
Transfer organoids from the Erlenmeyer flask to an ultra-low attachment 6-well plate using a 5 mL pipette.
Prune and separate organoids daily for the first week until they no longer stick together.
Maintain optimal density of 10-15 organoids per well.
Change media 2-3 times a week.
Check for neural retinal cells by week 18 to confirm post-mitotic state.
By week 24, examine for the formation of rudimentary outer segments on the outside of the organoid.
Ensure that outer segments are thick on the outside of the organoids by week 26-28 before performing toxicity assays.
Perform toxicity assay after week 26 when organoids have defined outer segments.
Prepare 1 mM stock solution of deoxySA in ethanol.
Store the deoxySA stock at -20°C for up to one month.
Dilute the 1 mM deoxySA stock solution to concentrations of 0.5 µM, 1 µM, and 2 µM in RDM+ medium.
Add 3 μL of ethanol to RDM+ to prepare a control treatment.
Under a dissection microscope, use a sterile probe to select 4 groups of organoids with at least 5 organoids per group.
Split the selected organoid groups into separate wells of an ultra-low attachment 6-well plate.
Aspirate off as much RDM+ from the organoids as possible.
Add one concentration of deoxySA in RDM+ to each well of organoids.
Add vehicle control to the fourth well of organoids.
Replace media with freshly prepared corresponding deoxySA dilutions in RDM+ after two days of culture.
Proceed to step 7 to process and assay organoids for cell death on the fourth day of treatment.
Prepare a 40 mM stock solution of fenofibrate in DMSO.
Store fenofibrate stock solution at -20 °C for up to 1 year.
In 3 mL RDM+, dilute 1 mM deoxySA stock solution to 1 µM deoxySA.
Dilute 40 mM fenofibrate stock solution to 20 µM in 3 mL RDM+.
Add 1.5 µL of DMSO to prepare deoxySA treatment media in 3 mL RDM+.
In 3 mL RDM+, add 3 µL ethanol and 1.5 µL of DMSO for control media preparation.
Select three groups of organoids with a minimum of five organoids per group under a dissection microscope using a sterile probe.
Split the selected groups into separate wells of an ultra-low attachment 6-well plate.
Add the prepared treatments (deoxySA, deoxySA + fenofibrate, or control) to the organoids.
After two days, change the media in the wells with freshly prepared RDM+ supplemented with corresponding deoxySA / fenofibrate / control solutions.
On the fourth day of treatment proceed to process and assay organoids for cell death.
Prepare fresh 4% PFA by adding 1 mL of 16% PFA ampoule to 3 mL of PBS.
Remove RDM+ media from organoids and rinse once with PBS.
Remove as much PBS as possible from organoids.
Add 2 mL of freshly prepared 4% PFA (in PBS) to the organoids and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Following 15 min incubation, rinse organoids twice with 2 mL of PBS.
Wash organoids in PBS for 10 min.
Aspirate all the PBS from the organoids.
Add 20% sucrose in PBS to the fixed organoids.
Ensure the organoids are mixed into the sucrose solution.
Keep the organoids in the sucrose solution until they sink to the bottom, approximately 1 hour at room temperature.
Store fixed organoids in sucrose solution overnight at 4 °C if needed.
Embed the organoids in OCT solution in a cryosection mold.
Orient the organoids so their best retinal regions will be cross-sectioned on the cryostat and the middle of the organoids are roughly in the same plane.
Freeze the embedded organoids at -20 °C.
Store embedded organoids at -80 °C for long-term storage if needed.
Cryosection organoids into 10-14 µm thick sections.
Adhere sections to poly-L-lysine treated slides.
Check the slides under a microscope repeatedly during cryosectioning to identify sections containing the middle of the organoids.
Collect only the middle slices where all layers are evenly represented.
Store sectioned slides in a slide box at -80 °C for long-term storage if needed.
Thaw frozen slides for 30 min at 37 °C.
Create a continuous border on the glass slide around the tissue sections using a hydrophobic pen.
Add approximately 100-200 μl of freshly prepared 4% PFA to the hydrophobic-bordered region and incubate for 20 min.
Rinse slides once in PBS then wash in PBS for 25 min at room temperature.
Prepare the TUNEL mixture by combining remaining violet vial solution with blue vial solution, mix well, and keep in the dark.
Permeabilize tissue slices.
Prepare Permeabilization Solution: PBS with 0.1% TritonX-100 and 0.1% Sodium Citrate.
Remove PBS from sample slides.
Add Permeabilization Solution to samples.
Incubate for 2 min on ice block or at 4 °C.
Rinse once in PBS.
Wash in PBS for 10 min.
Dry away as much solution as possible using the corner of a folded tissue.
Add 50-100 µL of prepared TUNEL mixture to the samples, depending on the size of the area drawn by the hydrophobic pen.
Cover with glass cover slip.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h in the dark.
Rinse once with PBS.
Wash for 20 min in PBS.
Remove PBS.
Add primary Recoverin antibody (rabbit anti-Recoverin) diluted 1:500 in PBS with 0.1% Tween and 5% donkey serum.
Incubate at 4 °C overnight.
Rinse once in PBS.
Wash in PBS for 20 min.
Add secondary antibody, donkey anti-rabbit with an orange or red fluorophore, diluted 1:1,000 in PBS with 0.1% Tween and 5% donkey serum.
Incubate at room temperature for 2 h.
Rinse once with PBS.
Wash for 20 min in PBS.
Add DAPI at 1:1000 in PBS.
Incubate at room temp for 10 min.
Rinse once with PBS.
Wash for 20 min in PBS.
Remove PBS.
Add mounting medium.
Add cover slip.
Seal with nail polish and leave to dry in the dark.
Store slides at 4 °C in a dark container for up to 1 week.
Locate retinal sections for imaging and quantification.
Use Recoverin staining to label the cytoplasm of photoreceptors.
Use DAPI staining to label the nuclei of all cells.
Identify an intact, well-formed region with a distinct outer nuclear layer of photoreceptors at least a few cells thick.
Find a separate layer of nuclei without Recoverin staining.
Increase magnification to 20x objective.
Frame the slide to fill the image with as much of the photoreceptor layer as possible.
Set the Z-plane for imaging.
Define the upper and lower limits of the Z-range to cover the entire depth of the slice if using a microscope that images Z-stacks.
Maintain consistent Z-stack thickness across all samples for uniform tissue assay measurement.
Focus on the middle of the slice if not using a microscope that images Z-stacks.
Image all three channels of fluorophores in a Z-stack acquisition.
Ensure all three channels are imaged to positively identify dying cells.
Capture one area per organoid.
Save image sets in a file format that preserves the ratio of area per pixel.
Open image stacks in FIJI (Image J) software.
Select 'Z project' from the dropdown menu under Image > Stacks to flatten the Z-stack image set for quantification.
Skip flattening step if organoids were imaged without a Z-series.
Select the image channel showing Recoverin staining.
Click on the polygon selection tool and outline a continuous region of photoreceptors.
Click on Analyze > Set Measurements, then select the box next to Area.
Measure the area of photoreceptors by clicking Measure or pressing "m".
Count TUNEL-positive nuclei in the photoreceptor region previously selected.
Right click on the point tool and select multi-point tool.
In the TUNEL channel, click on TUNEL positive staining overlapping with a DAPI positive nucleus and Recoverin staining.
Toggle between channels to validate positive cells.
Divide the number of TUNEL positive cells by the area to get a normalized value for cell death in photoreceptors per organoid.
